An event handler has to be a function. A string, a number, an object, an array or a class there is a mistake, often a missing arrow. The rule looks at `on:` directives and at attributes such as `onclick`, and follows a constant to the value it is declared with.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. It runs on the Svelte components that an ESLint config lints with `svelte-eslint-parser`, in the place of the rule of `eslint-plugin-svelte`:

{/* skip */}

```js eslint.config.js
import svelte from "eslint-plugin-svelte";

export default [
  ...svelte.configs.recommended,
  { rules: { "svelte/no-not-function-handler": "error" } },
];
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}

```svelte
<script>
  const save = "save";
</script>

<button on:click={save}>Save</button>
<button onclick={{ handleEvent: save }}>Save</button>
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}

```svelte
<script>
  const save = () => console.log("saved");
</script>

<button on:click={save}>Save</button>
<button onclick={save}>Save</button>
```
